q: 1. Surveys which are carried out to depict mountains, rivers, water bodies, wooded areas and other cultural details, are known as
explain: Surveys depicting natural features (mountains, rivers, water bodies) along with cultural/artificial details are known as topographical surveys.

q: 2. Angular surveying in which both horizontal and vertical positions of a point are obtained by optical means is known as
explain: Tacheometry is the branch of surveying that uses a telescope with stadia hairs to determine distances and elevations without a tape.

q: 3. If L is the measured length of a base line whose elevation is h above MSL, the necessary correction to reduce the base length to MSL is
explain: The standard correction to reduce a measured base line length at elevation h to mean sea level is given by L.h/R, where R is the mean radius of the earth.

q: 4. In the surveying telescopes, cross hairs are fitted in
options: optical centre of the eye piece
explain: Cross hairs in a surveying telescope are mounted on the diaphragm, positioned within the tube nearer to the objective lens (rather than near the eyepiece).

q: 5. In the surveying telescope, diaphragm is held
explain: The diaphragm (cross-hair mounting) inside a surveying telescope's tube is positioned nearer to the objective lens than to the eyepiece.

q: 6. The principle of working from whole to part is used in surveying because
options: survey work can be completed quickly
explain: Working from whole to part serves multiple purposes together - simplifying plotting, speeding up survey work, and preventing accumulation of errors - so all of these are valid reasons.

q: 7. The type of surveying which requires least office work is
explain: Since plane table surveying involves plotting directly in the field simultaneously with observation, it requires the least subsequent office work compared to other methods requiring separate field-book reduction and plotting.

q: 8. Surveys which are carried out to provide a national grid of control for preparation of accurate maps of large areas, are known
explain: Geodetic surveys are specifically carried out to establish a national grid of accurately positioned control points, accounting for the earth's curvature, for large-area accurate mapping.

q: 9. The main principle of surveying is to work
options: from higher level to the lower level
from lower level to higher level
explain: The fundamental principle of surveying is always to work from the whole (establishing an accurate overall framework first) to the part (filling in progressively finer detail).

q: 10. Systematic errors are those errors
options: whose effects are cumulative and can be eliminated
explain: Systematic errors are those whose character (cause, magnitude, and sign) is well understood and follows a definite mathematical/physical law, distinguishing them from random accidental errors.

q: 11. The difference in the length of an arc and its subtended chord on the earth surface for a distance of 18.2 km, is only
explain: For a distance of 18.2 km on the earth's surface, the difference between the arc length and its subtended chord length is extremely small, only about 1 cm, due to the earth's very large radius.

q: 12. In geodetic surveys higher accuracy is achieved, if
options: curvature of the earth surface is ignored
curvature of the earth surface is taken into account
angles between the curved lines are treated as plane angles
explain: Higher accuracy in geodetic surveys, which cover large areas, is achieved specifically by properly accounting for the earth's curvature in all computations, rather than ignoring it.

q: 13. Hydrographic surveys deal with the mapping of
explain: Hydrographic surveys are specifically concerned with mapping large water bodies - oceans, lakes, rivers, and harbours - including their depths and features.

q: 14. The instrument used to reproduce plans to a different scale is called
explain: A pantograph is the mechanical instrument specifically designed to reproduce plans and drawings at a different (enlarged or reduced) scale.

q: 15. To reproduce the given map to a small scale, positions of pointer and pencil in a pantograph are
options: pointer is to the longer arm and pencil to the shorter arm
pointer to the shorter arm and pencil to the longer arm
both pointer and pencil are to the two different short arms
both the pointer and pencil are to the two different long arms, pencil being fixed and pointer adjusted to the scale
explain: To reduce a map to a smaller scale using a pantograph, the pointer (tracing the original map) is set on the longer arm while the pencil (drawing the reduced copy) is on the shorter arm, giving a scaled-down reproduction.

q: 16. An important rule in using pantograph is
options: pointer, pencil and weight should fall in a straight line
pointer should never be put on the short arm
the arm on to which the weight is attached should never move
pencil is always attached to the arm on which the scale is marked
explain: A fundamental rule for correct pantograph operation is that the pointer, pencil, and the fixed pivot/weight point must always lie in a straight line for accurate proportional reproduction.

q: 17. The method of surveying in which field work and plotting work are done simultaneously called
explain: Plane tabling is uniquely characterized by simultaneous field observation and plotting on the table sheet, unlike other survey methods where plotting is done later in the office.

q: 18. Cross hairs in surveying telescope, are fitted
options: at the centre of the telescope
at the optical centre of the eye piece
in front of the eye piece
explain: As per the book's answer key, the cross hairs in a surveying telescope are described as fitted at the optical centre of the eyepiece assembly (diaphragm position within the eyepiece housing).

q: 19. An internal focusing type surveying telescope, may be focused by the movement of
explain: An internal focusing telescope achieves focus by moving an internal concave (focusing) lens back and forth within the tube, rather than moving the objective itself.

q: 20. The method of surveying used for determining the relative height of points on the surface of the earth is called
explain: Leveling, in its general definition, is the branch of surveying specifically used to determine the relative heights (elevations) of points on the earth's surface.
